scope: Bounded Chinese Warlords 1920/1930 identity and overview QA; 1938 geometry comparison only
geometryQualification: Two polygons include a sampled Hainan interior and exclude a sampled Taiwan interior. Bounds coincide. Raw geometry hashes differ; rounded vertex-set comparison is recorded rather than claiming byte-identical geometry. These are broad cartographic regions with separately labelled Tibet, Xinjiang and (1920/1930) Manchuria. 1938 has Empire of Japan rather than a separate Manchuria feature. No territorial or sovereignty reconciliation is inferred.

bodyLocators: Establishment of Subordinate Diplomatic Mission at Nanjing (Nanking), 1928
sources.evidence: Republican diplomatic relations resumed in May 1913. US recognition of the Nationalist government followed the July 1928 tariff treaty. Nanjing became that government’s capital in 1928. These are government facts, not proof that the mapped composite region was under uniform control.

sources.title: The Minister in China (Crane) to the Secretary of State
bodyLocators: paragraphs beginning Provincial troops and revenues / The military government at Canton
sources.evidence: The Peking government had contested institutions and rival military factions. Provincial governors largely controlled provincial troops and revenues. A Canton military government maintained a separate position. The report supports a composite political context, not a single warlord clique or uniform central authority.

sources.title: The Minister in China (Johnson) to the Secretary of State
bodyLocators: Peiping, February 19, 1930; report of conditions during January 1930
political situation paragraphs on Nanking Central Government and Yen Hsi-shan north of Yellow River
sources.evidence: The report distinguishes Nanking’s central government from powerful regional military authorities; Yen Hsi-shan controlled northern territory outside Manchuria. Suppression of revolts did not establish durable centralized control.

sources.title: The Minister in China (Johnson) to the Secretary of State
bodyLocators: sections on National Government and Nanking–Mukden relationship
October 21 entrustment of northern provincial administration
sources.evidence: The report describes improved National Government prospects after military victory while retaining provincial particularism and a negotiated division of northern administration with Mukden. This later observation must not be projected across all of 1930.

proposals.displayLabel: China — Peking government and regional military authorities
proposals.historicalContext: Beiyang-era republican government at Peking; the term Beiyang is an editorial period descriptor, not a formal name attested in the cited telegram.
proposals.overview: The mapped region represents much of mainland China and Hainan during a period of divided republican authority. In July 1920, the Peking government faced rival military factions, provincial governors controlled much of their troops and revenue, and a separate military government operated at Canton.
proposals.qualification: Composite map region, not one historical state or a single warlord clique. Separately mapped Manchuria, Xinjiang and Tibet and omitted Taiwan must remain outside this feature’s facts.

proposals.displayLabel: China — Nationalist government and regional military authorities
proposals.historicalContext: National Government at Nanjing (Nanking), alongside regional military authorities.
proposals.overview: The mapped region represents much of mainland China and Hainan amid Nationalist central-government claims and continued regional military authority. Reports from January and October 1930 describe contested power and changing military alliances, even as the Nanjing government strengthened its position later in the year.
proposals.qualification: Composite map region; no claim of uniform Nanjing control. The 1945–1960 existing Nationalist framework must not be silently extended backward to 1930.

coordinatorDecisionRequired: Approve qualified composite-region identity and snapshot-specific prose before any serial candidate integration. Government-context labels must remain distinguishable from sovereignty or territorial control.
